ratings_why.fun: Every turn asks who stands where and what fills the ground between stations, and the pieces chain (Brennbart blasts the Gallery that Wendelin eats, Reisig leaves so Einsiedel doubles twice); a few flat cards keep it at 7.
ratings_why.distinct: 8 over 7 because the board's own geometry is the tribe's puzzle: Knights blank each other, so the empty or filled slots between the three stations, often holding other tribes' units, are the real resource, and no current tribe plays like that.

verdict_why: The engine is good as is, but Squire and Watcher are printed on no card, so a player can't tell which units have them; label them and it can settle.

points.text: No card prints Squire or Watcher. The builds imply Konrad, Roost-Pine Squire and Rupprecht are Squires and Heather Hen, Bilberry Watcher, the Chronicler and Dame Reisig are Watchers; put the keyword on each card.
Bristlebeard says he 'takes' 2 Attack but not that he gains it; the builds assume he does. Say 'and gain it'.

Herald of the Old Lek doubles any Gallery unit's End of Turn effect, other tribes' included. That cross-tribe Brann is the best combo hook here; a second card that rewards specific outside units in the Gallery would lean into it.

Sir Brennbart can be switched off by parking a blank Knight next to him, and his blast can hit a waiting Squire. Worth one more card that likes its own Gallery dying, so the blast has a second payoff beyond Wendelin.
Pennon-Bearer is a plain buffer that spends a station; letting it buff only Knights it touches through a Gallery unit would make it another positioning puzzle.

standouts.why: Herald of the Old Lek turns any tribe's End of Turn units into Lek parts.
Dame Reisig doubles then leaves, and her leaving clears Einsiedel's slot for a second doubling: a combo the rule creates on its own.
Sir Wendelin sits where Brennbart's blast lands, so Gallery units are fuel twice over.

weakest.why: Pennon-Bearer does one obvious job and ignores the station geometry.
Edge-Strutter is a fine tempo body but has no second use.
White-Badge Knight is a plain Gallery buffer; it only matters through Bristlebeard and Brennbart.

flags.note: Heather Hens doubled by Herald of the Old Lek can pay a lot of gold a turn, more with goldens.
Rupprecht with the Chronicler gives +10/+10 to every Knight permanently each fight he takes Station; it repeats every round.
Doesn't say whether Bristlebeard gains the Attack he takes.
Squire Konrad doesn't print Squire, so it's unclear whether he blanks the elder he waits behind.
